title: Reconcile the weekly provider review without duplicating protocol or runtime
problem: OpenAI added provider-hosted computer use and beta multi-agent orchestration, OpenAI and Anthropic announced model retirement deadlines, and provider incidents affected collaboration surfaces. Decide whether UNIIMENTE needs new protocol law, a runtime migration, an evidence-only update, or no repository change.
baseline: Current default branches prefer local OpenAI-compatible inference and contain no Anthropic or Kimi runtime adapter. Draft PR 105 already proposes generic rules for provider sessions, tools, permissions, artifacts, retries, per-attempt cost, evaluator independence, data scope, and no duplicate runtime, but its branch is six commits behind main and contains a branch-only intent ID collision.

alternatives.name: Evidence-only reconciliation on draft PR 105
alternatives.description: Merge current main into the existing review branch, preserve prior provider records, correct the intent ID collision, add the dated evidence and deliberation, and add no new protocol invariant.
advantages: Preserves one review lineage and current founder doctrine
Records hard deadlines and direct-exposure negatives without policy duplication
Keeps every action reversible and consequence-inert
disadvantages: Adds review volume to an already large draft
Still depends on founder or independent human review before merge
alternatives.revival_evidence: Selected now; regress to brief-only when no hard deadline, direct exposure, new invariant, or branch-integrity defect exists.

alternatives.name: Add provider-specific browser and multi-agent protocol rules
alternatives.description: Extend the protocol with OpenAI-specific computer-use and subagent clauses.
advantages: Makes the newest provider terminology explicit
disadvantages: Duplicates existing generic leased-session, permission, cost, recovery, and no-second-runtime rules
Couples constitutional language to beta field names
alternatives.revival_evidence: A deterministic fixture exposes a browser or subagent authority/replay failure not covered by current generic rules.

alternatives.name: Immediate provider migration
alternatives.description: Switch collaboration or runtime routes to GPT-6.1 Sol or Claude Sonnet 5.5 now.
advantages: Could improve capability or retire future compatibility risk early
disadvantages: No direct affected route, benchmark, account contract, residency decision, or founder authorization exists
Could increase cost and create a second orchestration plane
alternatives.revival_evidence: Founder-approved sandbox evaluation with pinned contracts, independent acceptance, cost and residency evidence, and rollback.

alternatives.name: Provider-native orchestration owns collaboration
alternatives.description: Let hosted browser sessions and provider subagent trees own task state, retries, tools, and synthesis.
disadvantages: Violates canonical ownership and the no-duplicate-runtime constraint
Lets the provider route under test control evidence and evaluation
alternatives.revival_evidence: None while UNIIMENTE requires one canonical runtime, identity, authority, receipt, evidence, and cost plane.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Publish only the user brief and leave PR 105 unchanged.
advantages: Avoids touching a branch that diverged from main
disadvantages: Leaves hard retirement deadlines and new exposure evidence outside the durable record
Leaves the branch-only INTENT-0029 collision and six-commit drift unresolved

roles.position: Preserve the open-source-first and one-machine directions while keeping official provider options replaceable and reviewable.
material_concerns: A hosted provider feature must not silently become the project objective or stopping condition
The provider-review intent must not collide with the reserved Infinite Goal Chase identifier

roles.position: Use provider browsers, sessions, and subagents only behind the existing canonical runtime and contracts; add no duplicate provider-specific law.
material_concerns: Provider orchestration can create a second task and retry plane
Beta schemas and mutable provider models can break deterministic replay

roles.position: Prefer no repository change because all direct runtime searches are negative and PR 105 already covers the failure modes.
material_concerns: Weekly evidence accumulation can become bureaucracy and de facto policy
A model-authored review can overstate the materiality of prospective vendor features
evidence_refs: No direct Anthropic or Kimi runtime adapter

roles.position: Reconcile the existing draft with main once, record deadlines, and avoid any runtime or account action.
material_concerns: PR 105 is six commits behind main
Status surfaces can disagree in freshness and aggregate state
Future migrations need explicit owners and lead time
evidence_refs: OpenAI and Claude official status pages

roles.position: Keep credentials, browser sign-in, health-data eligibility, account balances, and residency outside this unattended review; require independent evidence before adoption.
material_concerns: Hosted browsers can expose sensitive data and account state
Provider credit and status messages do not prove a specific attempt or invoice state
The same provider cannot be the sole evaluator of its own orchestration

evidence.claim: OpenAI's hosted browser requires the application to handle approvals and sign-in and to recover the same session before retrying after a disconnect.
evidence.finding: The provider session is stateful and consequence-adjacent; blind restart can lose state or duplicate work.

evidence.claim: OpenAI Responses multi-agent is beta, lets a root model spawn a subagent tree sharing model and tools, may change item schemas, and can increase token use.
evidence.finding: It is an optional provider orchestration capability, not a replacement for canonical agent identity, authority, evaluation, or durable task state.

evidence.claim: OpenAI announced October 1 model and TTS deprecations with January 6 and April 1 shutdown dates.
evidence.finding: No affected identifier occurs on the four inspected default branches, but the deadlines require future authorized inventory before expiry.

evidence.claim: Anthropic will retire Claude Sonnet 4.5 from the Claude API on November 30, 2026.
evidence.finding: No Anthropic runtime or Sonnet 4.5 pin occurs on the inspected default branches.

evidence.claim: Current default branches use local OpenAI-compatible inference by default and expose no Anthropic or Kimi runtime.
evidence.reference: GitHub connector inspection: Kernel 19fa33c2, DALEOBANKS a8341ba8, WMI ec82b802, PumpStation db6758df
evidence.finding: Kernel is loopback-only; DALEOBANKS' paid OpenAI path is explicit and still uses gpt-4o-mini with optional text-embedding-3-small; WMI and PumpStation have no provider route.

counterevidence.claim: The weekly findings require another protocol rule.
counterevidence.finding: Existing generic rules already cover leased provider sessions/tools, dynamic capabilities, provider permissions, credential/data scope, per-attempt cost, independent evaluation, ambiguous recovery, and no duplicate runtime.

counterevidence.claim: A current runtime migration is necessary.
counterevidence.reference: Exact code searches on the four default branches observed 2026-10-06
counterevidence.finding: No newly deprecated model, Anthropic route, Kimi route, Agents API, Responses API, computer-use route, or multi-agent beta header was found.

pass_1.intended_outcome: Keep provider capabilities and collaboration surfaces replaceable, cost-auditable, retry-safe, and useful without allowing any provider to become a second canonical runtime, authority, evidence source, evaluator, or credential plane.

advantages.statement: An evidence-only update records hard deadlines and provider contracts without adding duplicate law.
advantages.amplified_value: Reviewers can act before retirement while the protocol remains provider-neutral and comprehensible.

advantages.statement: Reconciling PR 105 with current main preserves a single provider-review lineage.
advantages.amplified_value: Founder doctrine, open-source-first routing, and provider evidence remain reviewable in one non-production branch.

disadvantages.statement: Another weekly repository record creates review debt and may normalize policy accumulation.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Add no protocol text; record only hard deadlines, new provider orchestration contracts, direct exposure, and negative results. Return to brief-only when those conditions are absent.

disadvantages.statement: The deprecations are prospective and have no direct default-branch exposure.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Mark each as prospective, preserve exact shutdown dates, and prohibit migration until an authorized explicit pin is found.

disadvantages.statement: Hosted browser sign-in and saved activity can expose credentials, personal data, or regulated data.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Perform no browser/account action; require separate authorization, least privilege, retention/residency review, credential isolation, and deletion evidence before any canary.

disadvantages.statement: Provider multi-agent can become a second scheduler, task graph, and evaluator.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Treat every provider subagent as a subordinate leased attempt under canonical identities, grants, tools, cost, and independent evaluation; prohibit provider-owned durable orchestration.

disadvantages.statement: Aggregate and incident-specific provider status can differ in freshness and invite unsafe recovery conclusions.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Record observation time and source state, but recover only from canonical attempt receipts and a bounded canary.

disadvantages.statement: Reconciling a diverged branch can overwrite newer founder doctrine or preserve an intent-ID collision.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Use current main as the tree baseline, overlay only the reviewed provider artifacts, preserve both parent SHAs, and rename the provider intent to a collision-resistant date-based ID.

comparisons.baseline: PR 105 contains four dated reviews and robust generic provider rules but trails current main and uses the reserved INTENT-0029 identifier.
comparisons.do_nothing: Avoids new review debt but leaves hard deadlines and branch integrity defects unresolved in the durable review line.
comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: Publish a brief only; this is preferable on immaterial weeks but does not correct the current branch drift and identifier collision.
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: Let provider-hosted browsers and multi-agent sessions own state, retries, and evaluation; this reduces integration work but violates one-source-of-truth and no-duplicate-runtime constraints.
comparisons.reversible_experiment: Future offline fixtures can model session recovery, subagent usage, beta-schema drift, and model replacement without credentials, provider calls, or external effects.

rejected_alternatives.name: Add OpenAI-specific protocol clauses
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Existing provider-neutral rules already cover the material authority, replay, cost, and runtime risks.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: A deterministic failing case demonstrates a new uncovered invariant.

rejected_alternatives.name: Migrate models now
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: No direct affected route, account inventory, evaluation, or founder approval exists.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: Authorized exposure plus pinned fixtures, independent acceptance, residency and cost review, and rollback.

rejected_alternatives.name: Inspect provider accounts and credentials
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: The scheduled review is not authorized to access accounts, keys, balances, contracts, browser sessions, or invoices.

pass_2.attack_summary: The evidence-only design can still overclaim publication timing, overwrite main during reconciliation, treat one agent's five perspectives as independent review, or freeze a stale provider-status snapshot into apparent truth.

new_weaknesses.statement: A calendar-date review boundary can miss changes published after the prior run or double-count late updates.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Record exact observation time, source publication/effective dates, and prior-review baseline; classify uncertain timing explicitly.

new_weaknesses.statement: A branch reconciliation can silently regress current main content.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Construct the reconciled tree from current main, overlay only named provider artifacts, keep both commit parents, and verify the resulting comparison and CI.

new_weaknesses.statement: All five roles were performed by one model and are not independent approval.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Keep the PR draft, label the review non-independent, and require founder or delegated human review for merge or adoption.

new_weaknesses.statement: Status pages can update after evidence capture.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Preserve observation timestamps, distinguish incident-feed from aggregate state, and never use provider status as canonical attempt evidence.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Hard retirement deadlines, new provider orchestration contracts, and branch-integrity defects justify one evidence-only update; no protocol text is added.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Next weekly cycle; use brief-only unless the materiality gate is met

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: No migration occurs until an authorized direct model pin or route is identified.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Authorized exposure inventory or 60 days before the applicable shutdown

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: This review does not access or alter credentials, accounts, browser sessions, regulated data, or provider retention settings.
Provider subagents cannot own canonical task state, grants, tools, evaluation, or retries and cannot create a second runtime.
Provider status is stored only as time-bounded telemetry; canonical receipts govern recovery.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any provider incident or ambiguous completion

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: The branch is reconciled from the current main tree with an explicit two-parent commit, named overlays, collision-resistant intent ID, comparison verification, and CI.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any future main divergence or merge conflict

pass_2.final_design: Update draft PR 105 only. Reconcile it with current main, preserve all earlier provider evidence, rename the branch-only provider intent to INTENT-20260901-provider-change, add the 2026-10-06 review and validated deliberation, and add no new protocol text. Make no runtime, provider, model, account, credential, route, production, authority, or merge change.

residual_risks.risk: Live provider routes, account-selected models, balances, contracts, and residency settings remain unknown.
residual_risks.mitigation: Require a separate authorized-human inventory before migration or billing conclusions.
residual_risks.review_trigger: Before any live provider adoption or 60 days before an exposed shutdown

residual_risks.risk: The five-role review is one model's structured analysis, not independent approval.
residual_risks.mitigation: Keep the pull request draft and require founder or delegated human review.

residual_risks.risk: Official status and beta documentation can change after observation.
residual_risks.mitigation: Preserve dates and URLs, use pinned fixtures for adoption, and recheck status before a canary.
residual_risks.review_trigger: Next material provider update or canary proposal

dissent.handling: Preserve the Adversarial Reviewer's brief-only objection. The branch-integrity repair and hard retirement deadlines justify a dated evidence record, but the objection wins on policy scope: no new protocol rule, runtime fixture, provider call, or migration is added.

entries.position: Make no repository change because direct runtime exposure is negative and existing generic rules are sufficient.
entries.rationale: Recurring documentation can create review debt and falsely elevate prospective provider announcements into institutional policy.
entries.evidence_threshold: Future repository updates require a direct exposure, hard deadline, branch-integrity defect, or previously uncovered authority, replay, cost, privacy, or no-duplicate-runtime invariant.
entries.review_trigger: Founder review of PR 105 or the next weekly cycle

migration_plan: No runtime migration. If an affected model, hosted browser, Responses multi-agent feature, or Anthropic route is later proposed, first inventory the authorized direct exposure, pin the model/header/tool contract, add deterministic fixtures under canonical identities and receipts, perform independent evaluation, review retention/residency and credentials, set a cost ceiling, and run a founder-approved reversible canary.

steps: Leave draft PR 105 unmerged or revert the 2026-10-06 documentation-only merge commit
Preserve the dated evidence and dissent as historical records
Restore the prior PR head if branch reconciliation is found to have overwritten current main doctrine
Use brief-only reporting on a future cycle that does not meet the materiality gate

kill_criteria: Any default-branch write or merge without founder approval
Any live provider, model, route, credential, account, browser session, invoice, contract, or production change
Any provider-owned canonical workflow, identity, authority, memory, evidence, evaluator, receipt, or cost ledger
Any provider subagent or hosted browser expanding authority or bypassing consequence gates
Any second scheduler, durable provider session owner, retry daemon, or agent runtime
Any retry or failover without canonical receipt and idempotency reconciliation
Any model migration treated as replay-equivalent without fixtures and independent evaluation
Any unbounded or unapproved website access or sign-in
Any missing root/subagent/tool attempt cost or ineligible residency path
Any overwrite of newer main doctrine or unresolved intent-ID collision
review_trigger: Founder review of draft PR 105; any direct use of a deprecated model, OpenAI hosted computer use, Responses multi-agent, Anthropic Sonnet 4.5, Kimi route, or any provider incident with ambiguous completion
